title: The Virgin Mary and the Intercession of the Saints
author: Dn Yonnas
summary: The Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo doctrine concerning the Virgin Mary as Theotokos, ever-virgin, and the Second Heaven, and the Church's teaching on intercession — distinguishing the unique propitiatory mediation of Christ from the entreating intercession of the saints and the intercession of mercy shown to the poor.

sections.h2: The Virgin Mary in the Faith of the Tewahedo Church

sections.p: The Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church cherishes the name of the Virgin Mary as the Mother of God. This title is not the product of human thinking or invention but a divine declaration drawn directly from the Holy Scriptures. To confess Mary rightly is to confess her Son rightly, for what the Church says about the Mother is always for the sake of the truth about the Son who took flesh from her.

sections.h3: The Virgin Mary is the Mother of God (Theotokos)

sections.p: The prophets and evangelists witness that the Child born of Mary is God with us. The very name given through Isaiah declares this: the One conceived and born of the Virgin is Immanuel, "God with us." The Word who was in the beginning became flesh and dwelt among us, and that flesh He received from His mother. Because the One she carried and bore is true God, she is rightly and truly called the Mother of God.

sections.quote: Behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a Son, and shall call His name Immanuel.

sections.p: Scripture itself gives Mary this honor. When Elizabeth received the Virgin who carried the Lord in her womb, she was filled with the Holy Spirit and confessed Mary as the mother of her Lord, while the unborn John leaped for joy in worship of his God. The angels proclaimed to the shepherds that the One born was the Savior, Christ the Lord, and Gabriel announced to Mary that her Son would be called the Son of the Highest, reigning over an everlasting kingdom.

sections.quote: But why is this granted to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?

list: Isaiah's prophecy names the Child of the Virgin as Immanuel, God with us (Isaiah 7:14; Matthew 1:23).
The Word became flesh and dwelt among us, taking that flesh from Mary (John 1:14).
Elizabeth, filled with the Holy Spirit, calls Mary 'the mother of my Lord' (Luke 1:43).
The angels proclaim the newborn as 'a Savior, who is Christ the Lord' (Luke 2:11).
Gabriel foretells that her Son is the Son of the Highest whose kingdom has no end (Luke 1:32-33).

sections.p: The Church confesses the perpetual virginity of Mary. The angel Gabriel was sent to a virgin betrothed to Joseph, and her name was Mary. The Greek word for virgin, 'Eparthenos,' and the Hebrew 'Alma' carry the sense of perpetual virginity, for she gave birth to the Savior of the world and her virginity remained intact before, during, and after the birth.

The teacher recalls a traditional account of the Church: when the Virgin Mary entered the temple after giving birth to the Lord, she took her place in the rows of the virgins; when some tried to prevent her, Zechariah the priest told them to leave her there among the virgins, bearing witness that her virginity was undefiled. In the commemoration of the saints during the Divine Liturgy the Church confesses her as 'the Ever-Virgin Mary,' that is, the perpetual virgin.

A scriptural symbol of her unbroken virginity is the burning bush that Moses saw on the mountain. Just as the bush blazed with the fire of divinity yet was not consumed, so the womb of the Virgin became the carrier of the divine and human natures of the one Christ, and she was not burned by the divine nature she bore.

sections.quote: So he looked, and behold, the bush was burning with fire, but the bush was not consumed.

sections.h3: The Virgin Mary, the Second Heaven

sections.p: Heaven is the throne of God; because the Virgin Mary carried God within her, she is called the Second Heaven. The language of Scripture is striking: the Greek 'Episkiazo' (to overshadow) and the Hebrew 'Shakan' (to dwell) are the very words used for the dwelling of God in the tabernacle of the Old Covenant. The cloud that covered the tabernacle, so that the glory of the Lord filled it and Moses could not enter, expresses the same divine presence.

The same word for overshadowing appears at the Transfiguration, when the cloud overshadowed the disciples and the Father's voice declared, 'This is My beloved Son.' And it is precisely this word that Gabriel uses to Mary, teaching that the Holy Spirit and the power of the Highest would overshadow her, so that the Holy One born of her would be called the Son of God. Thus Mary becomes the living tabernacle, the new and second heaven in which God deigned to dwell.

sections.quote: The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Highest will overshadow you; therefore, also, that Holy One who is to be born will be called the Son of God.

sections.p: Intercession means mediation. A simple illustration helps: a person of influence pleads on behalf of another, presenting that person's request to a king or to someone of great power. In this picture are all the elements of intercession: a lowly petitioner who feels unworthy to ask directly, and a favored mediator whose standing helps the petitioner find grace in the eyes of the one who has power to grant the request.

The Church distinguishes three kinds of intercession in the spiritual life. These must never be confused, for the first belongs to Christ alone, while the others are the loving cooperation of the saints and the works of mercy by which we ourselves find favor with God.

There is one God and one Mediator between God and men, the Man Christ Jesus, who gave Himself a ransom for all. This propitiatory intercession is unique and unrepeatable: it belongs to Christ alone and to no creature. Human nature had perished and death had entered human life; the blood of Jesus poured out on the Cross is the price paid for sin, so that fallen man can stand before God without condemnation through faith in that blood. No saint, and not even the Theotokos, shares in this one redeeming mediation.

sections.quote: For there is one God and one Mediator between God and men, the Man Christ Jesus, Who gave Himself a ransom for all.

sections.p: Saint John likewise teaches that if anyone sins, we have an Advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous, who is Himself the propitiation for our sins and for the whole world. Every offering of the Old Testament was a symbol pointing to the one Offering made upon the Cross, as John the Baptist declared, 'Behold! The Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world.' In the Revelation, John saw those who benefited from this intercession of the blood of Jesus: they had washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.

sections.quote: And He Himself is the propitiation for our sins, and not for ours only but also for the whole world.

sections.h3: 2. Entreating Intercession — The Prayers of the Saints

sections.p: Because God loved us and called us His children, He taught the disciples to pray, 'Our Father who art in heaven.' Yet, as the teacher honestly asks, do we deserve to be called children of God when we live carelessly and fall repeatedly into sin? Having lost our favor as children through our many sins, we still pray boldly to God ourselves, and at the same time we ask the saints to pray for us. This is entreating intercession: not worship of the saints and not a rival to Christ's redemption, but the loving request that those who please God would join their prayers to ours.

So the Church sings in the hymn 'Rejoice O Mary,' confessing that we have no favor with our Lord except through her request and intercession, O our Lady the Mother of God. Scripture says, 'I honor those who honor me'; the Virgin Mary, the angels, and the saints have honored the Lord, and He honors them when they ask Him on our behalf. Their intercession is therefore wholly dependent on Christ and oriented to Him, never set up beside Him as a second redeemer.

sections.h3: Examples of Intercession from the Old Testament

list: Abraham interceded for Sodom and Gomorrah, and the Lord, who loved Abraham for his obedience, listened to him and was willing to spare the cities for the sake of even ten righteous people (Genesis 18:16-33).
Elisha the prophet prayed on behalf of his servant, asking the Lord to open his eyes that he might see the heavenly host, and again prayed for the eyes of the Syrian soldiers (2 Kings 6).

For the sake of David His servant, with whom God had a good relationship and of whom He said 'I found his heart according to my heart,' God did not divide the kingdom during the days of Solomon though Solomon had sinned.

sections.h3: Examples of Intercession in the New Testament

sections.p: The intercession of the Virgin Mary at the wedding at Cana of Galilee is the chief New Testament example. There the Lord performed His first miracle through her intercession, turning water into wine and turning sadness into joy, when the people at the wedding asked Mary to intercede for them. Saint Paul also asks the prayers of the Church, exhorting that supplications, prayers, and intercessions be made for all people, for this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Savior, who desires all to be saved.

sections.quote: I exhort first of all that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks be made for all men.

sections.h3: 3. The Intercession of the Poor — Works of Mercy

sections.p: Giving to and helping the poor is a great deed and a great intercession for us with the Lord our Savior. In the judgment scene of Matthew 25, the King welcomes the blessed of His Father because they fed Him when He was hungry and gave Him drink when He was thirsty, for whatever was done to the least of His brethren was done to Him. Mercy shown to the poor thus becomes a plea on our own behalf before God.

list: 'Inasmuch as you did it to one of the least of these My brethren, you did it to Me' (Matthew 25:34-46).
'He who has pity on the poor lends to the LORD, and He will pay back what he has given' (Proverbs 19:17).
'Make friends for yourselves by unrighteous mammon' (Luke 16:9).
'Blessed is he who considers the poor; the LORD will deliver him in time of trouble' (Psalm 41:1-3).

sections.p: The Church's teaching holds together two truths without confusing them. Christ alone is the unique propitiatory Mediator who ransomed us by His blood; this can never be shared with any creature. At the same time, the Church honors the Theotokos as Mother of God, Ever-Virgin, and Second Heaven, and asks the prayers of Mary, the angels, and the saints, while also storing up favor with God through mercy to the poor. To venerate the Mother and to seek the prayers of the saints is not to worship them but to glorify the one Lord who honors those who honor Him.
